conventions.convention: Restrictedness requires that, for every fixed vector v and current x, all modes with sufficiently large positive index annihilate v. It supplies no energy grading; the algebra is the loop central extension without the degree derivation.

The invariant form B makes long roots have square 2, and the adjoint Casimir acts as 2h∨ times the identity. A compact real form is additional input for the compact-basis formula, not an assumption needed to define h∨.
Normal ordering keeps J_x(r)J_y(s) when r<0 and reverses the factors when r≥0. Sugawara modes divide the quadratic sum by 2(k+h∨), requiring k+h∨≠0.

Positive-energy unitary modules are algebraic orthogonal sums over nonnegative integer energies, with finite-dimensional energy spaces, nonzero H_0, integral level k≥0, and compact adjoints X(n)*=−X(−n). Energy satisfies [E,X(n)]=−nX(n), corresponding to E=−d.
The Witt basis is d_m=−z^(m+1)∂_z, indexed by all integers, with bracket [d_m,d_n]=(m−n)d_(m+n); only finite Laurent-polynomial combinations occur.
The Virasoro central term is (m³−m)δ_(m+n,0)C/12 in the L_m convention.
A Virasoro highest-weight vector is nonzero, is killed by every positive mode, and is an eigenvector of L_0 and C. The generated module need not be irreducible or unitary.

load_bearing.statement: On any restricted affine-current module of complex level k with k+h∨≠0, [L_m,J_x(n)]=−nJ_x(m+n) for every x∈g and m,n∈Z. No grading, inner product, irreducibility, or integrability is required.
For a restricted affine-current module and any B-dual bases, each normally ordered quadratic mode Q_m is locally finite on every vector and independent of the chosen dual bases.

The adjoint Casimir for the normalized invariant form acts as a unique positive scalar γ_B times the identity; h∨=γ_B/2. For an additionally supplied compact real form and a −B-orthonormal basis X_i, −Σ_i ad(X_i)²=2h∨I.

On every restricted affine-current module of complex level k≠−h∨, [L_m,L_n]=(m−n)L_(m+n)+(c/12)(m³−m)δ_(m+n,0)I, where c=k dim(g)/(k+h∨). These modes and C↦cI define a Virasoro representation, without energy, unitarity, irreducibility, or integrability assumptions.
The bilinear form ω(d_m,d_n)=δ_(m+n,0)(m³−m)/12 is alternating and satisfies the Lie-algebra two-cocycle identity.
